summary.name: Maige
summary.one_liner: Maige is an open-source AI tool for running natural language workflows on a GitHub codebase, such as labeling, assigning, commenting on, and reviewing issues and PRs; the hosted service has been sunset.
use_cases: Auto-assign issues based on text rules
Review incoming pull requests against CONTRIBUTING.md
Flag or label PRs touching sensitive files like .env
Run simple code snippets in a sandbox from GitHub events
summary.what_it_does: Maige connects to a GitHub repository by creating a webhook, building embeddings of the whole codebase, and provisioning a sandbox environment. Users write rules in plain English describing what should happen when issues and PRs are opened. The AI can label, assign, comment on issues, review code, and run simple code snippets, using the GitHub API. Behavior is customized through text instructions, and a dashboard lets users monitor runs and give feedback. The page describes the project as open-source infrastructure, with the source kept on GitHub as a public archive.
notable: Plain-English rules that control labeling, assignment, comments, and PR review
Builds embeddings of the entire codebase and a sandbox environment on connect
Source remains open on GitHub as a public archive
caveats: The hosted service has been sunset and new signups are closed; only existing users can sign in
The page lists a paid Standard plan at $30/month with usage-based pricing, and an Enterprise tier marked coming soon
